title: Wedding Money and Home Visits: Tiyatien Health's First Year in Zwedru
conflicts: The slate's episode (training community health workers in 2007) does not match the record: the 2007 founding launched an HIV programme in Zwedru using lay accompaniers; Last Mile Health dates its community health worker pilot (Konobo) to 2012. The story tells the 2007 HIV founding and gives 2012 as what followed. Return to Liberia: about 2005 as a medical student (Panjabi on TED/NPR and HMS) vs TIME's 'in 2005 as a doctor' and HMS's 'returned in 2007 to found'; the story says fifteen years after 1990, as a medical student. National programme size differs (4,000+ planned, TIME 2017; about 3,500, NPR 2019) and is not given.
notes: Main contemporary source is Tiyatien Health's 2007 blog; the two posts quoted are signed by Raj, unsigned posts are used only for programme facts. Company field shortened to 'Tiyatien (later Last Mile)' because the repeat screen matched the word 'Health' to the 2007 Indus Hospital edition; prose uses full names. Stance 'complicates': Panjabi's own 2007 note said helpers could not replace doctors.
